chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: There was a Jewish boy who would come frequently to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) until he (the Prophet) grew fond of him. Sometimes he would send him on an errand, and sometimes he would have him write a letter to a people. Then he (the Prophet) missed him for some days and asked about him. Someone said to him: You have left him on the last day of his life in this world. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went to him with some of his companions — and among his (peace be upon him) blessings was that he could hardly address anyone without receiving a response. So he said: O so-and-so! The boy opened his eyes and said: At your service, O Abu al-Qasim! He said: Bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. The boy looked at his father, but his father said nothing to him. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called to him a second time and said the same as he had said the first time. The boy looked to his father but his father said nothing to him. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called to him a third time. The boy looked to his father, and his father said: If you wish, say it; and if you wish, do not. So the boy said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you, Muhammad, are the Messenger of Allah. And he died in his place. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his father: Leave us. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: Wash him and shroud him, and bring him to me so that I may pray over him.
Then he left, saying: Praise be to Allah who saved a soul from the Fire through me today.

key_terms.اسْتَحَبَّهُ: Grew fond of him, loved him; indicates deep affection the Prophet developed
key_terms.اشْهَدْ: Bear witness, testify; the invitation to the shahada
key_terms.بَرَكَة: Blessing, blessed grace; refers to the miraculous quality of the Prophet
key_terms.غُلَام: Boy, youth; in this context a young male servant or attendant
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service, here I am; a formula of joyful response
key_terms.نَسَمَة: A soul, a breath; poetic term for a human being

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do when a Jewish boy who served him was dying?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a moving account transmitted by Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about a Jewish boy who had developed a close relationship with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). When the boy was dying, the Prophet visited him and thrice invited him to testify to the Islamic shahada. After his father gave him permission to speak freely, the boy pronounced the shahada and died as a Muslim. The Prophet then instructed his companions to perform the funeral rites for the boy, departing with gratitude to God for having saved a soul from the Fire. This narrative illustrates the Prophet's profound compassion for all people regardless of religion, his eagerness to guide souls to salvation, and the Islamic principle that sincere acceptance of faith — even at the moment of death — is accepted by God.
